usage: 동생 = younger brother or sister. 남동생 = younger brother, 여동생 = younger sister.

examples.en: How old is your younger sibling?
My younger sibling is at school now.
My younger sibling is a Korean teacher.
My younger sister's name is Emma.
This is my younger brother's friend.

explain: 동생은 남동생도 여동생도 돼요. 형이나 언니는 동생을 '동생'이라고 부르지 않고 이름을 불러요. 동생은 형, 누나, 오빠, 언니라고 불러요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이 아닌, 친한 나이 어린 사람
phrases.nuance_en: a close friend who is younger than you but not family

phrases.en: to get a new baby brother or sister
phrases.nuance_en: said when a baby is born in the family
phrases.en_equiv: to get a new baby brother or sister

dict_examples.en: to get a younger sibling
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 장남인 그는 부모님 대신 어린 동생들을 데리고 힘겹게 살아갔다.
dict_examples.en: As the eldest son, he struggled to live while taking care of his younger siblings in place of their parents.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 동생 means a younger brother or a younger sister. Older siblings don't call the younger one '동생' — they use their name. The younger one calls them 형, 누나, 오빠 or 언니.

examples.en: There's a photo of my parents in my room.
My parents' house is in Seoul.
My parents are both teachers.
I'm buying a gift for my parents.
My friend's parents' house is on Jeju Island.

explain: 부모님은 아버지와 어머니 두 분을 함께 부르는 공손한 말이에요. “부모” 뒤에 높이는 말 “-님”이 붙었어요. “우리 부모님”이라고 자주 말해요.

dict_examples.en: to repay one's parents' kindness
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 부모님 is the polite word for father and mother together. It is 부모 (parents) plus the respectful ending -님. People often say 우리 부모님 (“our parents”) even when they mean their own.

examples.en: My younger brother is taller than me.
My younger brother is in the army now.
My younger brother is a middle school student.
My little brother's room is very small.
Do you have a younger brother? — No, I have a younger sister.

explain: 남동생은 “남자 + 동생”이에요. 그냥 “동생”이라고도 많이 말해요. 남자인지 여자인지 확실히 말하고 싶을 때 “남동생, 여동생”이라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: The older sister was proud of her younger brother who had been discharged from the military.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 남동생 is 남자 (male) + 동생 (younger sibling). People often just say 동생. Use 남동생 or 여동생 when you want to make clear whether the sibling is a boy or a girl.

examples.en: My younger sister is a student.
My younger sister lives in the US now.
My younger sister is a high school student.
My younger sister's name is Rena.
This is my younger sister's teacher.

explain: 한국어는 나이가 위인지 아래인지 꼭 말해야 해요. 여동생은 나이가 아래인 여자 형제예요. 나이가 위인 여자 형제는 “언니”나 “누나”예요.

dict_examples.en: He has two younger sisters.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Korean makes you say whether a sibling is older or younger. 여동생 is a younger sister. An older sister is 언니 (said by a woman) or 누나 (said by a man).

examples.en: My husband is American.
My husband is playing with the baby.
My husband's company is in Gangnam.
My husband is a chef.
My husband is at home now.

explain: 결혼한 여자는 '제 남편'보다 '우리 남편'이라고 많이 해요. 결혼한 뒤에도 남편을 '오빠'라고 부르는 사람이 많아요. 다른 사람의 남편은 '남편분'이라고 높여요.

phrases.nuance_en: a wives' pun joke: a husband is 'someone else's side' (남의 편)

dict_examples.en: to get a husband
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 결혼기념일을 맞아 남편과 여행을 가기로 했다.
dict_examples.en: For our wedding anniversary, I decided to go on a trip with my husband.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Married women usually say 우리 남편 (our husband) rather than 제 남편. Many still call their husband 오빠 after marriage. Someone else's husband is 남편분, to be polite.

examples.en: I bought flowers for my wife's birthday.
My wife and I first met at university.
My wife is a doctor.
My wife's name is Anna.
My wife is at the office now.

explain: 아내는 다른 사람에게 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 부를 때는 “아내!”라고 하지 않고 이름이나 “여보”라고 해요. 친구끼리는 “와이프”라고도 많이 말해요.

dict_examples.en: She became a man's wife.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The husband confessed everything to his wife.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 나는 내 힘으로 아내를 먹여 살리고 아이들을 키우고 싶소.
dict_examples.en: I want to support my wife and raise my children by my own efforts.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 아내 is what you say when talking about your wife to others. You do not call her 아내 to her face; use her name or 여보. Among friends, 와이프 (wife) is also very common.

dis.h: neutral standard word for own wife

p.n: 집사람 sounds humble and homey; 아내 is neutral.

examples.en: Ben is my coworker.
He's a colleague from work.
A colleague works together with me at the company.
My colleague is Korean.
Is that a colleague? — No, he's my friend.

explain: 동료는 다른 사람에게 소개할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 “동료!”라고 하지 않고 이름에 “씨”나 직함을 붙여요.

dict_examples.en: a coworker
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 동료 is a word for introducing or describing a co-worker. You do not call someone 동료 to their face; use their name plus 씨, or their job title.

examples.en: I go to my grandmother's house on weekends.
My grandmother's house is in Busan.
My grandmother's kimchi is really good.
Hello, Grandma.
My grandmother's hometown is Jeju Island.

explain: 할머니 집은 높여서 '할머니 댁'이라고 해요. 가족이 아니어도 나이 많은 여자 어른을 '할머니'라고 불러요. 하지만 젊어 보이는 분께 '할머니'는 실례예요.

phrases.example: 떡을 이렇게 좋아해요? 완전 할매 입맛이네요!
phrases.en: old-fashioned taste in food (lit. grandma's taste)
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 사람이 떡·나물 같은 옛날 음식을 좋아할 때 장난으로
phrases.nuance_en: said playfully when a young person likes old-fashioned foods like rice cakes and seasoned greens
phrases.en_equiv: old-fashioned taste in food (lit. grandma's taste)

dict_examples.ko: 그러면 지금 아버지는 할머니께 얼마씩 드리고 계세요?
dict_examples.en: Then how much does Father give Grandmother now?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Grandma's house is said politely as 할머니 댁. You can call any elderly woman 할머니, even a stranger, but calling someone who looks younger 할머니 is rude.

examples.en: Grandpa's glasses are here.
My grandfather's house is in the countryside.
Grandpa, this is my friend.
My grandfather's hat is really cool.
My grandfather's hometown is Gwangju.

explain: 할아버지는 아버지의 아버지와 어머니의 아버지에게 모두 써요. 구분하고 싶으면 아버지 쪽은 “친할아버지”, 어머니 쪽은 “외할아버지”라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 아이는 할아버지께서 직접 만들어 주신 연을 신나게 날렸다.
dict_examples.en: The child happily flew the kite that Grandfather had made himself.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 방학 때마다 시골 할아버지 댁에 간다.
dict_examples.en: He goes to his grandfather's house in the countryside every vacation.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Yeonam came to be raised by his grandfather.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 할아버지 is used for both your father's father and your mother's father. To tell them apart, say 친할아버지 (father's side) and 외할아버지 (mother's side).

examples.en: This child is my son.
My son is in high school.
My son is six years old.
Do you have a son? — Yes, I do.
My son's friend is American.

explain: 다른 사람의 아들을 높여서 말할 때는 “아드님”이라고 해요. 내 아들은 “아들”이라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: The father and son look like brothers.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The president handed over management of the company to his son.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Sons are rare in our family.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 재작년에 결혼한 친구가 아들을 낳았다는 소식을 들었다.
dict_examples.en: I heard that a friend who married the year before last had a son.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: When you talk respectfully about someone else's son, say 아드님. For your own son, just say 아들.

dis.h: plain word; usually your own son

p.n: The honorific form is for someone else's son, so it sounds wrong for your own.

examples.ko: 딸이 하나 있어요. 올해 일곱 살이에요.
examples.en: I have one daughter. She's seven this year.

examples.ko: 제 딸은 피아노를 정말 잘 쳐요.
examples.en: My daughter plays the piano really well.
My daughter's name is Hayun.
My daughter is a college student.
My daughter's friend is coming to our house.

explain: 한국 사람은 “제 딸”보다 “우리 딸”이라고 더 자주 말해요. 가족을 말할 때 “우리”를 많이 써요. 다른 사람의 딸을 높일 때는 “따님”이라고 해요.

phrases.en: a doting dad who adores his daughter
phrases.nuance_ko: 딸을 너무 아끼는 아빠, 좋은 뜻
phrases.nuance_en: a father who dotes on his daughter; a positive expression
phrases.en_equiv: a doting dad who adores his daughter

dict_examples.en: to give birth to a daughter
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to marry off a daughter
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 우리 집은 딸 둘, 아들 하나로 삼 남매입니다.
dict_examples.en: Our family has three children: two daughters and one son.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 자네 같은 사람한테 딸 안 주고 누구 주겠나.
dict_examples.en: Who would I give my daughter to if not a man like you?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Koreans say 우리 딸 (“our daughter”) more often than 제 딸, even for their own child. 우리 is the normal way to talk about family. To show respect for someone else's daughter, say 따님.

examples.en: How old is your child?
The kids are playing at the playground.
The child's name is Siu.
This child is my friend's daughter.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 아이가 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: My friend has one child.

explain: 아이는 내 아이에게도, 다른 사람의 아이에게도 써요. 말할 때는 “애”로 줄여서 많이 말해요. “애가 참 귀여워요”처럼요.

dict_examples.ko: 아니, 먹는 것을 가지고 어른이 아이를 울리면 어떻게 해요?
dict_examples.en: Oh no, what are you doing making a child cry over food, as an adult?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 놀이터에서는 고만고만한 아이들이 미끄럼을 탄다, 그네를 탄다 하며 떠들고 있었다.
dict_examples.en: At the playground, kids of similar size were making noise, going on the slide and the swings.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 아이 is used for your own child and for any other child. In speech it is often shortened to 애, as in 애가 참 귀여워요 (“the kid is so cute”).

p.n: 애 is the casual spoken shortening of 아이.

en: senior (someone who joined the same school or workplace earlier)

examples.en: Dain is my senior.
This is my senior from university.
Sunbae, let's have lunch together.
My senior's name is Jiho.
Is that a senior from school? — No, he's my friend.

explain: 선배는 이름 뒤에 붙여 “지호 선배”처럼 불러요. 더 공손하게 말할 때는 “선배님”이라고 해요. 학교나 회사에서 많이 써요.

dict_examples.en: a senior in the club
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: a senior at work
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to look up to someone as a senior
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: You call a senior by name + 선배, as in 지호 선배. To be more respectful, say 선배님. It is used a lot at school and at work.

en: junior (someone who joined the same school or workplace later)

examples.en: Minsu is my junior.
He joined the company after me.
Hubae, would you like some coffee?
My junior's name is Minsu.

examples.ko: 회사 후배는 일을 정말 열심히 해요.
examples.en: My junior at work works really hard.

explain: 후배는 나이가 아니라 학교나 회사에 들어온 순서로 정해요. 그래서 나이가 많아도 늦게 들어오면 후배예요.
explain_en: 선배 and 후배 depend on who joined first, not on age. So an older person who joined later is still a 후배.
